headline: Record bookings mask deepening losses and surging capex
summary_short: CoreWeave's Q1 FY2026 revenue more than doubled y/y to $2,078M and revenue backlog reached $99.4B on new agreements with Meta ($21B) and Anthropic, but GAAP net loss widened to $740M (net margin -36%) as capex surged to $7,695M, funded in part by an $8.5B DDTL 4.0 facility and a $2B NVIDIA equity investment.
summary_long: Revenue rose 111.6% y/y to $2,078M on new/expanded agreements with Meta ($21B), Anthropic, Cohere, Jane Street, and Mistral; revenue backlog reached $99.4B. Operating loss widened to $144M (margin -7% vs -3%) as technology-and-infrastructure costs rose 127% y/y, outpacing revenue growth. Adjusted EBITDA was $1,157M (margin 56%, down from 62% a year earlier). Net loss widened to $740M (-36% margin) on higher interest expense ($536M, from $264M). Capex rose to $7,695M (+447% y/y) funding data-center buildout past 1 GW active power. Financed via a new $8.5B non-recourse DDTL 4.0 facility and a $2B NVIDIA equity investment; cash fell to $2,244M (-28% q/q). No written guidance in this release — deferred to the earnings call.

drivers.explanation: CEO called this "the strongest bookings quarter in CoreWeave's history," with revenue backlog nearing $100B on new/expanded deals with Meta, Anthropic, Cohere, Jane Street, and Mistral, and active power surpassing 1 GW.
Growth driven by new/expanded customer agreements, including a $21B Meta commitment signed in March, a multi-year Anthropic deal, and expanded relationships with Cohere, Jane Street, and Mistral.
Margin compression is explained by technology-and-infrastructure costs rising 127% y/y to $1,273M and cost of revenue rising 173% y/y to $716M, both outpacing revenue's 112% y/y growth.
Company disclosed continued rapid scaling of AI infrastructure: active power surpassed 1 GW and total contracted power expanded by more than 400 MW to over 3.5 GW during the quarter.
Net loss widened mainly on higher interest expense ($536M vs $264M a year earlier) tied to increased debt funding the infrastructure buildout, on top of the wider operating loss.
Per-share loss narrowed slightly y/y despite a larger total net loss because weighted diluted shares roughly doubled (249M to 527M), diluting the loss per share.
